hero.headline: Oil Prices Drop as U.S.-Iran Agreement to Reopen Strait of Hormuz Takes Effect
hero.body:
Oil prices have fallen significantly after the United States and Iran reached a peace deal that will reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route that had been blocked for over 100 days. The agreement includes an end to fighting, a commitment that Iran will never develop nuclear weapons, and a 300 billion dollar redevelopment package for Iran.

The Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway between Iran and Oman, handles roughly one-fifth of global oil and liquefied gas supplies during peacetime. Its closure had severely disrupted global energy markets. Brent crude oil fell to lows of 82 dollars per barrel following the announcement, while wholesale gas prices dropped about 6 percent.

The reopening provides immediate relief to strained energy markets. Gasoline prices in the United States have begun to decline, with the national average falling below 4 dollars per gallon for the first time in months. The agreement removes a major source of uncertainty that had threatened to push energy prices even higher.

Financial markets responded positively to the news, with stock prices rising as investors welcomed the resolution of geopolitical tensions. The deal represents a significant diplomatic breakthrough between two nations that have long been at odds over regional security and nuclear issues.

However, industry analysts warn that broader price relief may take longer to materialize. Oil and gas prices are unlikely to return to prewar levels for months, even with the strait reopening. Markets are expected to remain elevated as buyers race to refill depleted emergency crude stockpiles that were drawn down during the crisis.

Jet fuel costs may remain particularly high for an extended period. Airlines and other industries heavily dependent on petroleum products will likely experience gradual rather than immediate benefits from the agreement. Flight prices may not fall quickly because fuel expenses represent only one component of airline costs, and carriers are aware that travelers are willing to pay premium prices for tickets.

The conflict that began on 28 February had disrupted energy production and transportation across the Middle East, causing fuel costs to spike globally. Countries in Asia that depend heavily on Gulf oil were particularly hard hit, facing shortages of fuel, fertilizer, and other raw materials. Even Western nations felt the impact, with Germany halving its 2026 growth forecast to 0.5 percent and Greece announcing 500 million euros in extra aid for households and farmers.

The International Maritime Organization reported that approximately 20,000 seafarers and 2,000 ships had been stranded in the Gulf as a result of the strait's closure. The reopening marks an important step toward stabilizing global energy markets and relieving the widespread economic pressures created by the extended disruption.

cards.headline: Ukraine Launches Largest Drone Strike on Moscow Since War Began
cards.body:
Ukraine struck Moscow with nearly 200 drones in what officials on both sides described as the largest aerial attack on the Russian capital since the full-scale war began in February 2022. The assault targeted an oil refinery and a shopping center in the southeastern part of the city, setting both facilities ablaze and forcing the closure of Moscow's airports for several hours.

The barrage focused on a major oil refinery in the Kapotno area, with the aim of shutting down its operations. A shopping center in the same region also caught fire during the attack. As drones moved toward their targets during the early morning hours, Russian air defense systems engaged the incoming aircraft. Explosions and fires became visible across the southeastern districts of the capital as the strike unfolded. The scale of the operation marked a significant escalation in Ukraine's campaign to strike deep inside Russian territory.

The attack disrupted transportation in the capital. Moscow's major airports suspended operations for several hours as authorities responded to the drone barrage, affecting both domestic and international flights. Russian officials activated air defense protocols across the capital region while emergency crews worked to contain the refinery fire. The damage to civilian infrastructure at the shopping center added to concerns about the scope of strikes being directed at Moscow.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the attack as a response to Russian strikes on a historic monastery complex in Kyiv earlier in the week. The assault appeared to surprise most Muscovites, as the city does not typically issue air raid warnings to residents, prompting panicked messages across social media.

Since the war began, Ukraine has increasingly targeted Russian energy infrastructure and military facilities far from the front lines as part of its strategy to degrade Russia's capacity to wage war. Earlier drone attacks on Moscow have been smaller in scale, typically involving dozens rather than hundreds of aircraft. The Kremlin has condemned such strikes as acts of terrorism, while Ukrainian officials argue they represent legitimate military operations targeting infrastructure that supports Russia's invasion.

The Moscow refinery represents a key piece of energy infrastructure serving the capital region. Its temporary shutdown could affect fuel supplies throughout the area. Ukraine has significantly expanded its domestic drone production capacity since the war began, allowing it to launch more frequent and larger strikes on targets inside Russian territory.

The attack occurred as fighting continued along a largely static front line in eastern and southern Ukraine. Both countries have faced mounting casualties and infrastructure damage as the conflict has persisted, with no clear end in sight despite ongoing diplomatic discussions about potential peace negotiations.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary orders review of US forces in Europe
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth announced a six-month review of American military presence in Europe and criticized NATO allies during remarks in Brussels.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a comprehensive review of US forces stationed in Europe during a visit to Brussels on Thursday, calling for a transformation of NATO into "NATO 3.0." Hegseth criticized allied nations, declaring an end to what he called the "era of free-riding" on American military support and emphasized that NATO must become a two-way street.

Hegseth made clear the review will have consequences for underperforming allies. He stated that some countries will "fail" the assessment while others will "pass with flying colours." US contributions to NATO will be contingent on other members meeting defense spending targets. The review aims to improve US force positioning while ensuring Europe assumes primary responsibility for its own defense.

cards.headline: Taiwan President Expresses Confidence in Trump Arms Sales
cards.teaser: President Lai says he trusts the incoming U.S. administration will approve a proposed $14 billion weapons package.
cards.body:
Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te said he trusts President-elect Donald Trump will approve arms sales to the island despite Trump's recent suggestion he might use the proposed package as leverage with Beijing. Lai made the remarks regarding a $14 billion arms deal currently under consideration.

Trump had publicly floated the possibility of using Taiwan's arms request as a bargaining chip in negotiations with China. The proposed weapons package represents one of the largest potential U.S. arms sales to Taiwan in recent years. Taiwan relies heavily on American military equipment to defend against potential Chinese aggression.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady as Officials Signal Possible 2026 Hike
cards.teaser: Stock futures rose after the Fed kept interest rates unchanged but more officials indicated higher rates could be the next move.
cards.body:
The Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged at its latest meeting, maintaining the range of 3.5% to 3.75% where rates have remained since December. The decision received unanimous support from the Fed's voting committee. Officials signaled that a rate hike could occur before the end of the year.

The committee noted that economic activity is expanding at a solid pace under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. US stock markets initially dropped following the announcement as investors processed the Fed's guidance on future rate moves.

cards.headline: Poll shows record low approval for Trump on economy
cards.teaser: A new national poll finds President Trump's job approval has reached its lowest point, with Americans expressing pessimism about economic conditions.
cards.body:
A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll shows President Trump's approval ratings have hit record lows as the nation heads into summer before the midterm election. Americans disapprove of his handling of the economy in particular, marking a significant shift in public sentiment on an issue traditionally important to his political base.

The decline in economic approval ratings presents a major challenge for the president. Voter assessments of economic performance typically influence midterm election outcomes, making these low numbers especially consequential heading into the election cycle.

cards.headline: Congressional Republicans break with Trump on key votes
cards.teaser: President Trump has expressed frustration as Republican lawmakers increasingly vote against his policy priorities.
cards.body:
Republicans in Congress have repeatedly broken ranks with President Trump on key legislative votes, frustrating the president's efforts to advance his agenda. Multiple GOP lawmakers have voted against measures backed by the White House, creating obstacles for the administration's policy goals.

The pattern of defections has drawn warnings from some Republicans that Trump's shifting focus could cost the party seats in upcoming midterm elections. The splits within the party reflect tensions over policy direction and legislative strategy as Republicans navigate differences between congressional priorities and White House demands.

cards.headline: Iran Secures Economic Relief in Initial Nuclear Agreement
cards.teaser: Tehran receives economic lifeline while deferring difficult nuclear concessions to future negotiations.
cards.body:
Iran reached an initial agreement that grants the country significant economic relief while postponing the most challenging nuclear restrictions to later talks. The deal provides Tehran with a crucial economic lifeline as it faces ongoing international sanctions.

The agreement allows Iran to delay major concessions on its nuclear program to subsequent negotiation rounds. The structure gives Iran immediate economic benefits in exchange for minimal changes to its current nuclear activities, setting up more contentious discussions for future diplomatic efforts.

cards.headline: Ugandan Opposition Lawyer Charged With Treason Offense
cards.teaser: Erias Lukwago faces charges after arrest earlier this week, with military chief promising harsh treatment.
cards.body:
Uganda's military chief publicly boasted of inflicting "hurt and pain" on lawyer Erias Lukwago before the opposition figure was arrested and charged with a treason-related offense. Lukwago represents Kizza Besigye, a prominent opposition politician who has repeatedly challenged President Yoweri Museveni.

The military leader's public threats preceding the formal charges have raised concerns about the integrity of the legal proceedings against Lukwago, highlighting broader pressure facing opposition figures and their legal representatives in Uganda.

cards.headline: Gunfire and Explosions Reported at Niger Airport
cards.teaser: Security incident at capital's airport follows January attack by suspected jihadists at the same location.
cards.body:
Gunfire and explosions were heard at the airport in Niger's capital. This marks the second major security incident at the facility this year, following a suspected jihadist attack in January.

Niger has faced a militant Islamist insurgency for the past decade, with violence spreading across the Sahel region. Multiple armed groups operate within the country despite the presence of security forces and international military support.

cards.headline: UK By-Election in Makerfield Could Trigger Leadership Crisis
cards.teaser: Vote could lead to Prime Minister Keir Starmer's removal from office depending on the outcome.
cards.body:
A parliamentary by-election in Makerfield is set for Thursday in northern England. The vote carries significant implications for Prime Minister Keir Starmer, with the potential outcome threatening his position in government.

By-elections gain heightened importance when a governing party operates with a narrow parliamentary majority or when political circumstances make results particularly consequential for party leadership. The Makerfield result could shift the balance of power in Parliament in ways that destabilize Starmer's premiership.

cards.headline: Suspected Gang Leader Killed in Flower Bouquet Ambush
cards.teaser: Gunmen concealed weapons behind flowers and stuffed toys at Guayaquil airport before shooting their target.
cards.body:
A suspected gang leader was shot and killed outside Guayaquil airport in Ecuador. Gunmen concealed their weapons behind flower bouquets and stuffed toys as they waited to ambush their target.

The killing underscores the escalating violence in Ecuador's largest city, where criminal organizations are fighting for control of drug trafficking routes. Guayaquil's position as the country's main port has made it a critical battleground in the cocaine trade.

hero.headline: Obama Presidential Center to be dedicated in Chicago
hero.body:
The Obama Presidential Center will hold its grand opening ceremony on Thursday in Chicago, marking the completion of a project that began nearly a decade after Barack Obama left office. The dedication event comes on the eve of Juneteenth and is expected to draw notable figures to celebrate the opening of the facility on the South Side of the city.

The center sits on a 19-acre campus in Jackson Park, close to where Obama lived as a young man and entered politics. The $850 million privately funded facility represents a significant departure from traditional presidential libraries. It includes a new branch of the Chicago Public Library, an NBA-regulation basketball court, a recording studio, and a sledding hill built because Michelle Obama never had one growing up on the city's South Side.

The museum showcases the legacy of former President Obama, highlighting his eight years in office and his impact on American politics and society. Unlike traditional presidential libraries operated by the National Archives, the Obama Presidential Center functions as a museum and community hub. The centerpiece is a 225-foot granite-covered monolith that houses the museum.

A defining feature of the center is its commissioned artwork. Barack and Michelle Obama commissioned original works by 30 artists from diverse backgrounds, a bold move never before seen at such scale at a presidential library. These artworks are dotted throughout the campus and interior spaces.

The art collection includes significant pieces such as Martin Puryear's monumental sculpture "Bending the Arc," inspired by Martin Luther King Jr.'s words about the arc of moral justice. Richard Hunt's "Book Bird," located in the library reading garden, depicts a bird bursting from book pages to evoke the emancipatory power of reading. This was Hunt's final work before his death in 2023.

Other notable artworks include an 83-foot-tall painted glass window by Ethiopian American artist Julie Mehretu titled "Uprising of the Sun," and a mixed-media portrait of Barack and Michelle Obama by Nigerian American artist Njideka Akunyili Crosby. Mark Bradford's "City of the Big Shoulders" is a 38-foot-tall textured painting mapping Chicago and Lake Michigan.

According to Valerie Jarrett, chief executive of the Obama Foundation, the Obamas wanted visitors to engage with art in meaningful ways. "We want people who come here to look at a piece of art, stand next to a stranger, have a conversation about that piece of art and how it touches them each in their own individual ways," Jarrett said.

The opening marks the beginning of public access to the center, which organizers hope will become a significant cultural and educational destination in Chicago. The facility aims to engage visitors with interactive exhibits and programming related to the Obama presidency and broader themes of American democracy and civic participation.

cards.headline: Great American State Fair to open on National Mall
cards.teaser: A 16-day event will feature booths representing all US states and territories, though several state governments have declined official participation.
cards.body:
The Great American State Fair will open on the National Mall as a 16-day event featuring booths representing all U.S. states and territories. According to organizers, every state and territory will have a presence at the fair, even where official state government participation is absent.

Several state governments have declined to officially participate in the event, which aims to celebrate America's approaching 250th anniversary by showcasing regional cultures and state-specific attractions in one location.

cards.headline: Jet fuel prices drop but airfares remain high
cards.teaser: The average price of jet fuel has fallen to its lowest level since the start of the Iran war, but ticket prices are not expected to decline.
cards.body:
Jet fuel prices have fallen to their lowest level since the war with Iran began. Despite this decline in one of airlines' major operating expenses, aviation experts say airfares are unlikely to drop anytime soon.

Airlines continue facing other rising costs and are working to recover from accumulated financial pressures. These factors mean carriers are likely to maintain current ticket prices even as fuel costs decrease.

cards.headline: Museum expands accessibility for 250th anniversary visitors
cards.teaser: A museum is working to make historical artifacts more accessible to people with disabilities as the nation marks its 250th year.
cards.body:
As America approaches its 250th anniversary, one museum is expanding efforts to make history accessible to visitors with disabilities through touch-based exhibits. Federal law requires museums and public buildings to provide physical access for people with disabilities, but access to exhibits and collections themselves often remains limited.

The museum's approach allows visitors to physically interact with historical materials, going beyond the traditional look-but-don't-touch model. The initiative reflects growing recognition that meaningful access extends beyond building entrances and requires rethinking how collections are presented and experienced.

cards.teaser: President Trump has expressed frustration as Republican lawmakers increasingly vote against his policy priorities.

Republicans in Congress have repeatedly broken ranks with President Trump on key legislative votes, frustrating the president's efforts to advance his agenda. Multiple GOP lawmakers have voted against measures backed by the White House, creating obstacles for the administration's policy goals.

cards.headline: SpaceX Stock Surges in Trading Debut as Retail Investors Drive Demand
cards.teaser: Individual investors pushed SpaceX shares sharply higher in the company's first day of public trading.
cards.body:
SpaceX made its stock market debut on the Nasdaq with a valuation of $2.2 trillion, marking the largest IPO ever. The blockbuster listing was driven by strong demand from retail investors, who have become increasingly influential in shaping market outcomes. Founder Elon Musk, who previously gave the company less than a 10% chance of success, oversaw the historic public offering from Texas.

The company's rapid ascent to become one of the world's most valuable corporations reflects both investor enthusiasm and the growing power of individual traders. Financial advisers caution that investing in single stocks carries substantial risk, even for prominent companies like SpaceX, and recommend investors carefully consider their risk tolerance before committing significant capital.

cards.headline: Apple Plans Price Increases as AI Chip Costs Rise
cards.teaser: The technology company will raise prices on products as the artificial intelligence boom drives up semiconductor costs.
cards.body:
Apple will raise prices across its product lineup due to surging costs for advanced computer chips driven by artificial intelligence development. Outgoing CEO Tim Cook announced the decision but did not specify which products would be affected or provide a timeline for implementation.

The AI boom has intensified demand for cutting-edge semiconductors, straining supply chains and increasing manufacturing costs across the technology industry. Apple is among major manufacturers adjusting pricing to reflect these rising input costs tied to the race for AI capabilities.

cards.headline: U.S. Job Vacancies Fall to Five-Year Low
cards.teaser: The number of open positions dropped to its lowest level in five years as companies grow cautious about hiring.
cards.body:
Job vacancies in the United States fell to their lowest level in five years, according to new government data. The figures suggest that companies are becoming more cautious about taking on new staff amid economic uncertainty.

The decline in job openings represents a shift in the labor market after a period of intense competition for workers. Businesses appear to be slowing their hiring plans as they assess economic conditions and adjust to changing demand for their products and services. The cooling in job vacancies could signal broader changes in employment trends across multiple industries.

cards.headline: India Temporarily Bans Telegram Messaging App
cards.teaser: India joined several other countries in restricting access to the encrypted messaging platform.
cards.body:
India temporarily banned the Telegram messaging app, adding to a growing list of countries that have restricted the platform. Telegram has become a valuable communication tool for dissidents, criminals, and extremists due to its encryption features and relatively light content moderation.

Several nations have moved to limit or block access to Telegram over concerns about illegal activity and content dissemination on the platform. The app's encryption makes it difficult for authorities to monitor communications, creating tensions between privacy advocates and governments seeking to regulate online activity. India's ban follows similar actions by other countries grappling with how to balance security concerns against communication freedoms.

cards.headline: Flight Ticket Prices May Stay High Despite Lower Oil Costs
cards.teaser: Airlines may keep ticket prices elevated even as fuel costs decline following the U.S.-Iran agreement.
cards.body:
Air travelers may not see immediate relief from high ticket prices despite falling oil costs following the U.S.-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Jet fuel prices are expected to remain expensive for months, limiting the potential for fare reductions.

Airlines also recognize that travelers have demonstrated willingness to pay higher prices for tickets, reducing the pressure on carriers to lower fares even as their fuel costs decline.

hero.headline: NASA awards Mars mission contract to Eric Schmidt's Relativity Space
hero.body:
NASA has selected Relativity Space to develop a Mars orbiter mission through a new public-private partnership, establishing competition with SpaceX in the race to explore the red planet. The rocket company, which was acquired by former Google executive chair Eric Schmidt last year after struggling to reach orbit, received the contract to privately develop the Aeolus Mars mission.

This partnership represents a shift in NASA's approach to Mars exploration, combining government scientific objectives with private sector execution. Relativity Space will design and build an orbiter to conduct scientific research from Martian orbit as part of the arrangement.

Relativity Space had faced significant obstacles before Schmidt's acquisition, including difficulties achieving orbit with its rockets. The company specializes in 3D-printed rocket manufacturing, a production method designed to reduce costs and timelines for space launch vehicles. Schmidt's investment has provided the company with renewed capital and strategic direction.

SpaceX has long been the dominant private sector player in Mars exploration discussions. CEO Elon Musk has repeatedly stated ambitions to establish human settlements on Mars, and the company has conducted numerous cargo and crew missions to the International Space Station for NASA. SpaceX also developed the Starship vehicle intended for deep space missions. NASA's decision to partner with Relativity Space introduces a new competitor into the Mars mission development landscape.

The Aeolus mission reflects NASA's broader strategy of leveraging commercial partnerships alongside government resources. The space agency has increasingly turned to private sector companies for both Earth orbit operations and deep space exploration, aiming to reduce mission costs while expanding capabilities. This approach represents a continuation of a strategy that has proven successful in lower Earth orbit activities.

For Relativity Space, the contract represents a significant step forward. The company must now demonstrate that its technology can support interplanetary missions, a major advancement from Earth orbit operations. The mission will test the company's manufacturing innovations and engineering capabilities at a scale not previously attempted by the organization.

The timing of this announcement comes as NASA grapples with challenges across its broader exploration programs. The space agency has been working to refine its technology development approach and address technical issues affecting multiple missions. By partnering with established private sector companies like Relativity Space, NASA appears to be distributing risk and leveraging external expertise to advance its long-term exploration goals.

The Aeolus mission contract positions Relativity Space as a serious contender in deep space exploration and demonstrates NASA's confidence in the company's 3D-printing technology for advanced space applications. The partnership will likely influence how future Mars missions are structured and developed.

cards.headline: Epic announces Unreal Engine 6 will merge UE5 and Fortnite creation tools
cards.teaser: The next version of Epic's game development platform will combine its traditional engine with Fortnite's creator tools into a single system.
cards.body:
Epic Games unveiled Unreal Engine 6 at State of Unreal 2026, consolidating Unreal Engine 5 and the Unreal Editor for Fortnite into a single platform. The company simultaneously released Unreal Engine 5.8, featuring optimization enhancements that will form the foundation for the next major version.

The company has invested $1 billion in payments to developers building content through UEFN, its Fortnite creation system. Epic is also enabling cross-game compatibility for Fortnite character skins, allowing cosmetic items to be used across other games developed with the engine.

cards.headline: Apple CEO warns AI costs may force iPhone price increases
cards.teaser: Tim Cook described current pricing as unsustainable as the company integrates artificial intelligence features into its devices.
cards.body:
Apple's outgoing CEO Tim Cook has indicated the company may raise prices due to costs associated with artificial intelligence capabilities. Cook described the situation as unsustainable, though he did not specify when price increases would occur or which products would be affected.

The comments reflect broader industry pressures as technology companies invest heavily in integrating AI features into consumer devices. These advancements require more powerful processors and computational resources, driving up manufacturing expenses across the sector.

cards.headline: Archaeologists discover 5,000-year-old structure near Stonehenge aligned with solstices
cards.teaser: The simpler monument consisted of two posts positioned three miles from the famous stone circle.
cards.body:
Archaeologists have uncovered a 5,000-year-old monument at Bulford, three miles from Stonehenge, that was aligned with the summer and winter solstices. Carbon dating places the structure around 3000 BC, coinciding with Stonehenge's earliest construction phase. Wessex Archaeology describes the discovery as a "once in a lifetime find."

The monument may have served as a prototype for Stonehenge's later solar alignments. It predates by 500 years the massive trilithon stones at Stonehenge that were positioned to track the midsummer and midwinter sun, suggesting that astronomical observation held significance for prehistoric communities across the region's landscape.

cards.headline: NASA astronauts photograph aurora australis from International Space Station
cards.teaser: Crew members captured views of the southern lights glowing beneath the orbiting laboratory.
cards.body:
Astronauts aboard the International Space Station captured stunning images of the aurora australis dancing beneath them. The photographs showcase the southern lights glowing beneath the orbiting laboratory as it passed overhead.

The footage reveals the shimmering auroral display as viewed from the station's unique vantage point in low Earth orbit. The aurora australis occurs when solar wind particles interact with Earth's magnetic field and collide with atmospheric gases, producing the distinctive luminous glow visible from high latitude regions.

cards.headline: FDA approves second fly species for medical maggot therapy
cards.teaser: The carcass-eating larvae join an existing species cleared for wound treatment despite limited clinical data.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration cleared a second species of carcass-eating fly for use in maggot therapy to treat wounds. The larvae consume dead tissue in wounds, a practice that has attracted supporters despite a lack of robust clinical trial data.

Maggot therapy uses sterilized fly larvae to clean wounds by eating necrotic tissue while leaving healthy tissue intact. Medical practitioners have used the treatment as an alternative to surgical debridement in certain cases, particularly for patients with wounds that resist conventional healing methods.

cards.headline: Google Docs adds option to disable Gemini AI writing prompts
cards.teaser: Users can now turn off the 'write with Gemini' pop-ups that appear in documents.
cards.body:
Google added a setting allowing users to disable AI writing suggestions that appear in Google Docs. The feature removes the 'write with Gemini' pop-up prompts that the company integrated into its document editing platform.

Users can access the option through their Docs settings to prevent the AI assistant from offering writing suggestions during document creation. Google introduced Gemini AI features across its productivity suite as part of a broader push to integrate artificial intelligence into workplace tools.

hero.headline: Liverpool trigger release clause to sign winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna
hero.body:
Liverpool Complete First Signing Under Iraola with Munoz Deal

Liverpool have activated Victor Munoz's £34.5 million release clause to secure the Osasuna winger as the first signing of Andoni Iraola's managerial reign. The club moved swiftly to beat Newcastle United to the Spanish player's signature.

The 22-year-old will sign a six-year contract after completing a medical examination on Wednesday in Atlanta, where he is currently part of the Spain squad at the World Cup. Liverpool had been monitoring Munoz's development for some time before accelerating their interest following Iraola's appointment.

The new head coach was particularly keen to bring in his fellow Spaniard, having spent most of his playing career at Athletic Bilbao and maintaining close connections with La Liga. Manchester United and Bayer Leverkusen also expressed interest in the winger, while Barcelona and Real Madrid had shortlisted him during their own recruitment processes before deciding to pursue alternative targets.

Munoz's versatility will be a key asset for Liverpool moving forward. The winger can operate on either flank or as a central striker, providing Iraola with tactical flexibility as the club enters a new era. His pace is considered one of his primary strengths, aligning with Liverpool's transfer strategy this summer to recruit players with significant speed.

The young player has already earned two caps for Spain, scoring in his debut against Serbia in March. He was an unused substitute in Spain's subsequent match against Cape Verde before joining Liverpool's setup.

The signing will not influence the future of Federico Chiesa at the club. The Italian winger was used sparingly under previous manager Arne Slot but could be better suited to Iraola's tactical approach. Chiesa remains eager to secure regular first-team football and is open to departing if opportunities remain limited.

Meanwhile, Liverpool have confirmed the departure of defender Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid. The centre-back will join on a four-year contract when his current Liverpool deal expires at the end of June. Real Madrid have also strengthened their squad significantly this summer, having appointed Jose Mourinho as head coach and subsequently recruiting Marc Cucurella and Bernardo Silva.

The Munoz transfer represents a statement of intent from Liverpool under their new management, with the club willing to invest significantly in attacking talent. At 22 years old, he represents both immediate quality and long-term potential as Iraola begins reshaping the squad to compete across the Premier League and European competitions.

cards.headline: Caroline Harvey selected first overall by Vancouver in PWHL Draft
cards.teaser: The Vancouver Goldeneyes chose Caroline Harvey with the first pick in the 2026 Professional Women's Hockey League Draft.
cards.body:
Vancouver selected Harvey at the top of the draft, making her the highest-selected player in this year's entry draft. The first overall pick represents a significant moment for both Harvey and the Goldeneyes franchise as they build their roster.

The draft also saw Detroit select Swiss goaltender Brndli, Boston choose Grace Dwyer in the first round, and Toronto take Plymouth's Kirsten Simms with the eighth overall selection. The draft brought new talent into the league as teams continue to develop their rosters for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Ronaldo held scoreless as Portugal draw with DR Congo at World Cup
cards.teaser: Portugal were held to a surprise draw by DR Congo while Cristiano Ronaldo struggled to find the net.
cards.body:
Portugal drew 1-1 with DR Congo in their World Cup match, failing to capitalize on their favorites status. João Neves gave Portugal an early lead, but Yoane Wissa equalized for DR Congo, who secured their first-ever World Cup point.

The result contrasted with other top performers in the tournament's opening round. While superstars like Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappé and Vinícius Jr. delivered memorable goals for their nations, Ronaldo could not find the net for Portugal, leaving them with just a draw instead of the victory they had expected.

cards.headline: Colombia defeat Uzbekistan in World Cup return
cards.teaser: Colombia marked their return to the World Cup with a victory over tournament debutants Uzbekistan, with Diaz scoring.
cards.body:
Colombia made a winning return to the World Cup, defeating World Cup debutants Uzbekistan 3-1 in Mexico City. Luis Díaz was instrumental in the victory, scoring and providing an assist that earned him man of the match honors. Daniel Muñoz added a brilliant strike to Colombia's tally.

Jefferson Lerma, Colombia's Crystal Palace midfielder, controlled the center of the pitch and helped dominate much of the match. Despite Colombia's superiority, Uzbekistan mounted a spirited challenge under manager Fabio Cannavaro. The result gives Colombia a strong start to their group stage campaign.

cards.headline: England defeat Croatia 4-2 despite defensive concerns
cards.teaser: England produced attacking football in their 4-2 victory over Croatia, though defensive vulnerabilities emerged during the match.
cards.body:
England made a winning start to their World Cup 2026 campaign with a 4-2 victory over Croatia in Dallas. The match proved thrilling, with England demonstrating strong attacking play to secure all three points against their old rivals.

Manager Thomas Tuchel made tactical adjustments for the match, including selecting Jude Bellingham over Morgan Rogers and adapting England's pressing approach to counter Croatia's style of play. The victory came after England's preparation at their pre-tournament camp, setting a positive tone for their campaign.

cards.headline: Salford City appoint Peter Cklamovski as manager
cards.teaser: Salford City named Peter Cklamovski as their new manager despite his lack of experience coaching in English football.
cards.body:
Salford City have appointed Peter Cklamovski as their new manager, tasking him with leading the League Two club to promotion. Notably, Cklamovski brings no prior experience of coaching in English football to the role, marking an unconventional appointment for the club.

Cklamovski has previously worked alongside manager Postecoglou and employs a data-driven coaching approach. His appointment reflects Salford's ambition to implement fresh strategies as they seek to climb out of League Two.

cards.headline: Xander Schauffele identified as strong contender for U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills
cards.teaser: Xander Schauffele's consistent play positions him well for the challenging conditions expected at Shinnecock Hills for the U.S. Open.
cards.body:
Schauffele has been highlighted as a player with the game suited to handle the windy and difficult conditions at Shinnecock Hills. His consistency could prove valuable on a course known for testing even the best golfers in demanding weather.

The U.S. Open field also includes Scottie Scheffler and Jon Rahm among the top contenders. Shinnecock Hills is expected to present a severe test with strong winds potentially turning the tournament into a battle of survival rather than aggressive scoring.

hero.headline: Daveigh Chase, Voice of Lilo and Star of The Ring, Dies at 35
hero.body:
Daveigh Chase, the actress and voice performer known for bringing Lilo to life in Disney's 2002 animated film Lilo & Stitch and for playing the ghostly Samara Morgan in the horror film The Ring, has died at age 35. Her boyfriend, Roy Hernandez, confirmed that she died from meningitis and blood infections that led to sepsis.

Chase had been hospitalized in Los Angeles earlier this month after being admitted for malnutrition. Her condition deteriorated as the infections took hold, and she passed away on Tuesday. Before her death, Hernandez had set up a GoFundMe page seeking assistance, describing Chase's struggles and his desire to provide her with a safe home during her final days.

Born on July 24, 1990, in Las Vegas, Nevada, Chase began her entertainment career as a child actor. Her dual roles in 2002 demonstrated her range as a performer, moving seamlessly between family-friendly animation and dark horror. Her voice work as Lilo Pelekai became iconic in animation, while her portrayal of the long-haired ghost who emerges from a television screen in The Ring became one of the most memorable images in modern horror cinema.

Beyond these two most recognizable roles, Chase built a substantial career in film and television. She voiced Chihiro Ogino in the English dub of Studio Ghibli's Spirited Away and appeared in several other notable projects including the cult film Donnie Darko and the television series Sabrina the Teenage Witch. Her voice work connected to Lilo & Stitch extended to related projects and sequels throughout her career.

According to her longtime manager, Chase had faced significant hardships behind the scenes. In statements to media outlets, the manager noted that despite her successful film work, she had struggled with personal difficulties. Hernandez's GoFundMe message described how Chase had endured a challenging childhood and a painful estrangement from her family. He spoke of her experiencing bullying and struggling to find stability while living in downtown Los Angeles.

Hernandez characterized Chase as someone who "has always been a light" in his life, and expressed his commitment to providing her with the love and comfort she deserved during their time together. Before her condition became critical, they had found moments of happiness and hope.

Chase's death marks the early end of a career that began with significant promise and delivered performances that continue to reach audiences across generations and genres. Her work as Lilo brought warmth and humor to a story about family and belonging, while her contribution to The Ring helped define horror cinema for a new generation of viewers. The entertainment world has lost a performer whose roles became embedded in popular culture.

cards.headline: Lil Nas X Says He Is Feeling Better After Rehab and Bipolar Diagnosis
cards.teaser: The Old Town Road performer addressed his mental health following treatment and a diagnosis.
cards.body:
Lil Nas X has said he is feeling better after completing rehab and receiving a bipolar diagnosis. The artist, whose breakout hit Old Town Road became a cultural phenomenon, entered treatment following an arrest last year.

The arrest involved charges related to attacking police officers. Lil Nas X subsequently entered rehab to address his mental health. His public statement about his condition marks a notable moment of openness from the performer about his personal struggles.

cards.headline: Joel and Ethan Coen to Receive Lumière Award at Festival in Lyon
cards.teaser: The filmmaking brothers will be honored at the 18th edition of the festival in October.
cards.body:
Joel and Ethan Coen will receive the Lumière Award at the 18th edition of the Lumière Festival, which runs from October 10 to 18 in Lyon, France. The festival, headed by Cannes chief Thierry Frémaux, focuses on classic cinema and iconic filmmakers.

The Coen brothers have built a distinctive career in American cinema with films spanning multiple genres. Their work has earned them recognition at major film festivals and awards ceremonies worldwide. The Lumière Festival honor adds to their list of accolades for contributions to filmmaking.

cards.headline: Netflix Announces K-Pop Demon Hunters Immersive Experiences in Dallas and Philadelphia
cards.teaser: The ticketed experiences will open at Netflix House locations this holiday season.
cards.body:
Netflix has announced that K-Pop Demon Hunters: The Immersive Experience will come to Netflix House locations in Dallas and Philadelphia. The announcement comes on the film's one-year anniversary, with the ticketed experience set to open at both locations this holiday season.

Fan screenings of K-Pop Demon Hunters are scheduled for June 20 at both Netflix House locations. The immersive experience represents Netflix's continued expansion of its physical entertainment offerings tied to its streaming content.

cards.headline: Kaiser Chiefs Singer Ricky Wilson to Play Teen Angel in Secret Cinema's Grease Production
cards.teaser: Wilson joins the cast of the immersive musical running from July through September in London.
cards.body:
Ricky Wilson, frontman of Kaiser Chiefs, has been cast as Teen Angel in Secret Cinema and TodayTix's return staging of Grease: The Immersive Movie Musical. The production will run at Evolution London in Battersea Park from July 22 to September 13.

Wilson joins a cast that includes Girgios Michaeldes as Danny and Archangelo Ciulla as Kenickie. The immersive production represents Secret Cinema's approach to bringing classic films to life through interactive theatrical experiences that place audiences within the world of the story.

cards.headline: London Museum Smithfield Site to Open in November
cards.teaser: The building will house works including a Banksy piece and historic documents.
cards.body:
The London Museum Smithfield site will open in November, providing a new home for notable works including Banksy's piranhas artwork. The site will also house the UK's oldest hand-written document.

The opening represents a significant addition to London's cultural infrastructure. The Smithfield location will serve as a venue for both contemporary and historical pieces, bringing together artifacts spanning centuries of British history and culture.

cards.headline: Women in Animation Announces 10th Anniversary Summit at Annecy Festival
cards.teaser: The summit will feature producer Bonnie Arnold in a fireside chat.
cards.body:
Women in Animation has announced its lineup for this year's WIA World Summit at Annecy, themed Frame by Frame: A Global Celebration of Women and Nonbinary Creators. The summit marks 10 years of the event and will feature producer Bonnie Arnold, who will take part in a fireside chat.

The organization is also looking ahead to what comes next for the summit as it reaches this milestone anniversary. The event at Annecy, one of the world's premier animation festivals, provides a platform for celebrating and supporting women and nonbinary creators in the animation industry.

hero.headline: Trump blocks Republican priorities as Senate frustration mounts
hero.teaser: Republican senators say the White House is interfering with legislation they want to pass, including reauthorization of a foreign surveillance law.
hero.body:
Republican senators are increasingly frustrated with the White House's interference in their legislative agenda. The tensions are particularly acute on issues requiring Democratic support to overcome Senate filibuster rules, including efforts to reauthorize a lapsed surveillance law that allows intelligence agencies to monitor foreign threats.

Beyond domestic legislation, Senate Republicans have also criticized Trump's foreign policy moves. Several GOP senators have sharply attacked the administration's interim deal with Iran, with one calling it "the worst foreign policy blunder in decades." The agreement, which reopened the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for sanctions relief, has generated significant skepticism among Republicans concerned about concessions made to Tehran.

cards.headline: Gas prices fall below $4 per gallon after Iran ceasefire
cards.teaser: The national average gas price dropped below $4 per gallon as crude oil prices fell to their lowest levels in over three months.
cards.body:
The U.S. national average gas price has dropped below $4 per gallon, according to AAA, offering relief to consumers after extended price increases. The decline follows a ceasefire agreement between the U.S. and Iran that reopens the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil transportation.

Oil prices fell to their lowest levels in months following the ceasefire announcement. The conflict, which began in late February, had disrupted energy production and transportation across the Middle East, driving fuel costs higher. With the strait reopening, gas prices are expected to stabilize, though they may remain elevated compared to pre-conflict levels.

cards.headline: Trump refuses to drop voter ID bill despite Senate opposition
cards.teaser: The president continues pushing the SAVE America Act voting bill even as Senate Republicans say it cannot pass.
cards.body:
President Trump is refusing to abandon the SAVE America Act, a voting bill focused on voter ID and proof of citizenship requirements, despite repeated signals from Senate Republicans that it will not pass. The president's insistence on the legislation highlights a disconnect between the White House and congressional vote-counting realities.

Trump posted on Truth Social that he would not allow the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act to be renewed until his demands are met. The position shows how the president's unwillingness to accept Senate constraints is carrying consequences for other legislative priorities, including national security measures that many Republicans want to advance.

cards.headline: Trump approval rating hits record low in new poll
cards.teaser: A record low share of Americans approve of President Trump's job performance and his handling of the economy, according to polling.
cards.body:
A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll shows President Trump's approval rating has reached a record low as the country heads into summer before the midterm election. Americans also gave historically low marks for his handling of the economy.

The survey reflects broader voter concerns during a challenging period for the administration. The timing of these low approval numbers could pose difficulties for Republicans in the upcoming midterm contests.

cards.headline: White House AI policy team in flux as key advisers depart
cards.teaser: David Sacks is stepping back from daily involvement while Siriam Krishnan prepares to leave the administration.
cards.body:
The Trump administration's AI policy team is undergoing significant changes as key figures reduce their involvement. David Sacks is stepping back from day-to-day responsibilities while Siriam Krishnan is preparing to leave his position. Both had served as primary architects of the administration's AI agenda.

As these officials depart, influence over AI policy is dispersing to a broader group within the White House. The shifts occur amid rapid advances in AI technology that continue to present new policy challenges for the government.

cards.headline: House members struggle in bids for higher office
cards.teaser: Members of Congress who chose to run for Senate or governor instead of seeking reelection are losing primaries at a high rate.
cards.body:
House members who opted to run for higher office rather than seek reelection have had a poor track record this year, with primary losses potentially exceeding recent historical rates. The defeats have occurred despite members having advantages like national profiles and established fundraising networks.

The high rate of primary losses suggests that congressional experience may not provide the electoral boost that candidates expect when running for Senate seats or governorships. The trend could influence future decisions by House members considering whether to pursue higher office or remain in their current positions.

cards.headline: Trump administration shapes AI industry without formal regulations
cards.teaser: The White House says it opposes AI regulation but is influencing the industry through case-by-case interventions.
cards.body:
Trump's shadow AI policy

The Trump administration entered office promising to keep government out of the AI industry's way. Instead, it has shaped the sector through case-by-case interventions while rescinding Biden-era AI policies.

This ad hoc approach has created what observers call a shadow AI policy—influencing how companies operate and plan for the future without establishing clear formal rules. The lack of transparent guidelines has left AI companies uncertain about how the government will respond to different situations.
